question.text: The general solution of the differential equation, $\sin 2 x\left(\frac{d y}{d x}-\sqrt{\tan x}\right)-y=0$, is :

solution.text: Given, $\sin 2 x\left(\frac{d y}{d x}-\sqrt{\tan x}\right)-y=0$ or, $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y}{\sin 2 x}+\sqrt{\tan x}$ or, $\frac{d y}{d x}-y \operatorname{cosec} 2 x=\sqrt{\tan x}$ Now, integrating factor (I.F) $=e^{\int-\operatorname{cosec} 2 x}$ or, I.F $=e^{-\frac{1}{2} \log |\tan x|}=e^{\log (\sqrt{\tan x})^{-1}}$ $=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\tan x}}=\sqrt{\cot x}$ Now, general solution of eq. (1) is written as $$ \begin{aligned} &\text { y (I. F.) }=\int \mathrm{Q}(\text { I.F.) } d x+c \\ &\therefore y \sqrt{\cot x}=\int \sqrt{\tan x} \cdot \sqrt{\cot x} d x+c \\ &\therefore y \sqrt{\cot x}=\int 1 . d x+c \end{aligned} $$
